Description: The proposed ADR-003 (I11 SECURITY DEFINER Governance) and ADR-004 (EC8 Audit Chain) use numbers reserved by ADR-INDEX section 2.1/2.2 for the informal-ADR reconciliation map (RC4 ADR-01 -> TBD-P3 (ADR-003); RC4 ADR-02 -> TBD-P3 (ADR-004); reservations continue through ADR-017 for Phase5). ADR-001 section 2.1(3) states 'a number is never reused'; Governance Freeze EC10 = 'no informal-ADR numbering collision'. If the ADRs are registered as 003/004 without a Board resolution, the Phase-3 renumbering of RC4 ADR-01/02 collides and the series violates its own numbering policy.
Mitigation: Resolve the numbering BEFORE registration: recommended R1 - assign these decisions the next free numbers ADR-018/ADR-019 (leaving the RC4/Phase5 map intact and satisfying EC10); or an explicit Board re-sequencing. Update file names, ADR headers, ADR-INDEX references, and the submission accordingly.

Description: ADR-004 sections 2(3) and 3.3 cite PQ1-EC8-final-confirmation.md as supporting the traceability-chain Candidate A. That document resolves a DIFFERENT EC-8 question (Document aggregate subscriber endpoint, its own Candidate A/B) and cites a non-existent source file (domain-model/object-model.md - no domain-model/ directory exists). For a decision whose subject is traceability (T3), a mis-cited evidence chain is a provenance defect in the constitutional record and could mislead the Board and future audits. The same conflation appears in ADR-BOARD-C6-PQ1-FINAL-READINESS.md line 22.
Mitigation: Remove the PQ1-EC8-final-confirmation.md citation from ADR-004 section 2(3)/3.3 (or correct it to cite only the verified constitutional sources: object-model section 2.3 line 107 and enforcement-architecture section 2/3); correct FINAL-READINESS line 22; re-verify before Board acceptance. The Candidate-A selection itself remains supported by the two verified constitutional sources.

Description: ADR-004 sections 3.1/5/6 claim the audit-chain edges are 'records, examines, constrained-by' (backward). At the vocabulary level (relationship-kinds.ts): records has validTo = [Verification, Gate] (cannot connect Decision->Evidence); examines and constrained-by are forward forms (backward readings are the inverse pairs is-examined-by and constrains); and there is NO direct registered Decision->Evidence edge - the hop is established through the recorded provenance projection (records/produces via Verification/Gate). If the future engine builds the EC8 audit scaffold against the stated edge list, it risks range-incompatible links (the exact class RSK-02/HIGH-2 was created to prevent).
Mitigation: Reword ADR-004 to describe the chain as a backward traversal (traverses, line 61) over the audit chain, with an explicit hop-edge contract for the engine: Evidence->Constraint via is-examined-by, Constraint->Rule via constrains, Decision->Evidence via the recorded provenance projection. Pin this in the audit-chain edge assertions (test set) before engine design.

Description: The exception scope is pinned to the 28-function inventory, but the prior-package artifacts enumerate system.fn_auto_transition (SECURITY DEFINER per backend/schema_only_dump.sql:213; present in 5 of the 6 counted schema dumps) as part of the surface. fn_auto_transition was dropped (archive/sql-history/39-drop-auto-transition.sql; Workflow-Implementation-Contract.md marks REMOVED) and is excluded from the final audit inventory that ADR-003 cites. If the live Gate-0 baseline differs from the 28-function enumeration at R9-record time, the exception scope would not match the repository (PREC-04).
Mitigation: Before creating the R9 exception record, mechanically enumerate the live Gate-0 baseline and confirm it contains exactly the 28 enumerated functions (and not fn_auto_transition); record the reconciliation in ADR-003 or the exception record; any divergence is a violation until sanctioned.

Description: ADR-003 section 2.3(1) states all 28 live functions 'bypass RLS on protected data', but the audit's own section 2 Q1 records that system.fn_current_user_id (C6-005) reads only the app.user_id GUC and is 'unnecessary hygiene, NOT an RLS bypass'. The 28-function scope is conservatively safe, but the causal sentence overstates the bypass surface, which could be used to over-justify future bypasses or confuse the bypass-detection verification.
Mitigation: Add a precision note: 27 of 28 in-scope functions access RLS-protected data; C6-005 is hygiene-only and is included conservatively in the scope. Align the bypass-detection verification (R4) with the 27-real-bypass + 1-hygiene split.

Description: ADR-003 section 12 item 5 records the precedence/conflict-resolution requirement 'per the later enforcement work'. PREC-02 requires the precedence rule recorded in ADR text and a test green before Phase 4. Read literally, section 12(5) could defer the precedence recording entirely, understating what the Board must close on acceptance.
Mitigation: Anchor section 12(5) to the precedence statement already made in ADR-003 section 5(1) (recorded on acceptance), clarifying that only the enforcement-level encoding (specification/relationship level) is deferred to the later enforcement work.

Description: Both ADRs deviate from the binding template section numbering (template: section 1 Context, 2 Decision, 3 Alternatives, 4 Consequences, 5 References) using custom sections (ADR-003: 1 Metadata..13 Board Decision Template; ADR-004: 1 Context..9 Board Decision Template). All required content is present; the structure is not. Strict template conformance is a registration requirement (ADR-001 section 2.2).
Mitigation: At registration, either map the custom sections to the template headings in a compliance table or restructure to the template order; confirm no content is lost.

Description: Both ADRs correctly state that acceptance alone does not authorize Phase 4 (ADR-003 section 11; ADR-004 section 8). Residual risk: a reader or later implementer treats acceptance of the ADRs (or the R9 record) as Phase-4 authorization. The Phase-4 gate remains AND: C6 + PQ-1 closed, artifacts updated, governance test set green, and the later architectural review confirming C1-C6 closure (DECISION-P3-001 section 4; DECISION-P3-002 section 2), then a separate Board authorization decision.
Mitigation: Keep the 'does not authorize Phase 4' language in both ADRs; record the gate in the Board decision minutes and in the Phase-4 authorization decision itself; do not accept any Phase-4 work on the strength of these ADRs alone.

Description: The prior decision package and the authoritative final audit diverge on the enumerated surface (C6EV-10 includes fn_auto_transition; the final audit inventory does not) and on the EC-8 question (PQ1-EC8-final-confirmation vs ADR-INDEX PQ-1). Both ADRs correctly cite the final audit, but the repository contains two partially inconsistent evidence chains that could confuse later Phase-3/Phase-4 audits.
Mitigation: Record the final audit as the authoritative surface source; annotate the prior-package rows (C6EV-10; FINAL-READINESS line 22) as superseded; reconcile in the evidence register before Phase 4.
